facts: Q1 2026 net sales declined 3.2% to $1.4 billion with adjusted EPS of $0.32, both ahead of guidance but reflecting continued underlying business pressure.
Full-year 2026 guidance was reaffirmed at net sales down 4.5% to down 2.5% and adjusted EPS of $2.40–$2.65, with no share repurchases, no tariff refund benefit, and assuming elevated energy prices.
Q2 guidance calls for net sales down 5% to down 3%, gross margin of ~40%, SG&A rate of ~31.8%, and EPS of $0.20–$0.25, with Q3 expected to see greater transformation investment.
Body Care declined mid-teens, materially below the rest of the shop, driven by over-pulled-back everyday luxury assortment (now restocked with 10 fragrances) and accessory mix in Disney Princesses 2.
Adjusted gross margin fell 270 bps to 42.7%, with merchandise margin down 210 bps largely from ~130 bps of tariffs, inflation, and crude oil pressure plus category mix.
Mix-adjusted AUR was flat year-over-year, but new moisturizing/revitalizing soap launches delivered double-digit AUR and SKU productivity gains, sustaining into replenishment.

Amazon launch is delivering strong double-digit week-over-week growth with higher AURs than owned channels and a younger, more affluent new-to-brand customer skew, currently at ~94 SKUs (~7% of in-store assortment).

International retail sales grew double digits despite Middle East conflict pressure; Q2 international net sales are expected down low- to mid-single digits due to shipped product declines to the Middle East partner.
CFO Eva Boratto is departing; Tom Javich (16 years at BBW) will serve as interim CFO while an external search is underway, with management asserting no change to guidance confidence.

Company expects ~$600M of free cash flow in 2026 (including a $66M after-tax interchange litigation benefit), $270M of capex, redeemed $284M of January 2027 notes in Q1, and returned $40M via dividends; inventory ended Q1 down 10%.
Full year 2025 adjusted EBITDA was $69.7 million, representing 53% growth over 2024.
Full year 2025 comp sales were down 0.3% (excluding deferred loyalty revenue), with a 3.5% increase in average check offset by a 3.8% decrease in traffic.
Fourth quarter 2025 comp sales were down 3.3% (excluding deferred loyalty revenue), with a 0.3% increase in average check and a 3.6% decline in traffic.

The company's 2026 guidance includes comparable restaurant revenues of 0.5% to 1.5%, restaurant-level operating profit margin of approximately 13%, adjusted EBITDA of $70 million to $73 million, and capital expenditures of $25 million to $30 million.
A 3.2% menu price increase was implemented with the new menu rollout at the end of January 2026 and is expected to carry through the full year.
Labor efficiency initiatives contributed approximately 180 basis points to restaurant-level margin in Q4 and drove a 250 basis point reduction in total labor costs for full year 2025.
G&A expenses (excluding stock-based compensation) were reduced by over $4 million in 2025 to $71 million, with a further reduction to $65 million-$67 million expected in 2026.
The company terminated its at-the-market equity offering program with no shares issued, citing improved business performance and progress in refranchising work.
Quarter-to-date Q1 2026 comps are down about 1%, with weather impacts estimated to cost approximately 50 basis points in total Q1 comp and approximately 179 operating days lost.
Commodity inflation is expected to be approximately 4% in 2026, similar to 2025, driven primarily by beef inflation while other major categories are expected at plus or minus 1%-2%.
Consolidated Q3 2025 revenue was $152.5 million, down from $171.8 million in the prior year period, primarily due to softening customer demand in North America.

The company lowered full year 2025 revenue guidance to $640 million to $650 million from prior guidance of $650 million to $670 million, and adjusted EBITDA guidance to $17 million to $19 million from $21 million to $25 million.

Global Electrical Systems segment revenues increased 6% year-over-year to $49.5 million, driven by the ramp-up of new business wins with an autonomous vehicle manufacturer in North America and a major automotive manufacturer in Europe.
Year-to-date free cash flow reached $25 million, up $14 million from the prior year, and the company expects to generate at least $30 million of free cash flow for the full year to pay down debt.
Net leverage ratio increased to 4.9x at quarter end, up from 4.8x at the end of Q2, with a target to return to 2x through 2026.
Adjusted gross margin improved to 12.1%, representing a cumulative improvement of 370 basis points versus Q4 2024, despite an 11% sequential revenue decline.
The Trim Systems and Components segment revenue declined 29% year-over-year to $34.3 million, underperforming relative to the 39% year-over-year decline in Class 8 builds according to ACT Research.

Interest expense increased to $4.1 million from $2.4 million in Q3 2024 due to higher interest rates following the June 2025 debt refinancing, adding approximately $1 million to $1.5 million per quarter.
The company expects Global Electrical Systems segment sales to increase in the high single-digit to low double-digit percentage range in 2026, despite weaker end markets.
SG&A run rate has been reduced from approximately $20 million per quarter to $17 million per quarter, representing a 15% year-over-year reduction.
Q1 2026 consolidated pretax income was $798 million on $6.9 billion of revenues, resulting in a pretax profit margin of 11.6%.
Earnings per diluted share for Q1 2026 were $2.03, compared to $2.61 in the prior year quarter.
Net sales orders increased 3% year-over-year to 18,300 homes, while order value remained unchanged at $6.7 billion.
The company repurchased 4.4 million shares of common stock for $670 million in Q1, and outstanding share count is down 9% from a year ago.
Home sales gross margin was 20.4%, but excluding a 40 basis point benefit from a warranty cost recovery, the margin would have been 20.0%.
Q2 2026 guidance includes home sales gross margin of 19% to 19.5%, reflecting increased incentives used throughout Q1.
Full year fiscal 2026 guidance remains at consolidated revenues of $33.5 billion to $35 billion and 86,000 to 88,000 homes closed.
Housing starts in Q1 were 18,500 homes, up 27% sequentially from Q4, with management expecting Q2 starts to be higher than Q1.
Completed unsold homes inventory declined by 2,000 units from September to 7,300 at quarter end.
The average number of active selling communities increased 12% year-over-year and 2% sequentially.
Q1 2026 revenue exceeded $2.7 billion with 3% currency-neutral sales growth, led by mid-single-digit growth in Health & Biosciences and low single-digit growth in Taste, Food Ingredients, and Scent.
Adjusted operating EBITDA rose 8% to $568 million and EBITDA margin expanded 110 basis points to 20.7%, the highest level since Q2 2022.
IFF reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance of $10.5–$10.8 billion in sales (1–4% growth) and adjusted operating EBITDA of $2.05–$2.15 billion (3–8% growth), with FX expected to add ~1 point to sales.
Management explicitly guided Q2 2026 EBITDA to be below the $568 million reported in Q1, citing moderated growth, unfavorable price-to-input costs, and Fine Fragrance weakness in the Middle East.
Free cash flow improved by $144 million year-over-year to $92 million in Q1, with operating cash flow of $257 million (up $130 million YoY) and CapEx of $165 million (~6% of sales).
Gross debt fell more than $3 billion year-over-year to $5.85 billion, with net debt to credit-adjusted EBITDA at 2.5x on trailing EBITDA of approximately $2.1 billion.
The company completed the divestiture of its commodity soy crush, concentrates, and lecithin business to Bunge for $110 million on March 2, one month ahead of schedule.

The Food Ingredients sale process has multiple potential buyers in second-round due diligence, with an update expected by the Q2 earnings call; the segment delivered double-digit EBITDA growth in 2025 and Q1 2026, with EBITDA margins building from 9% in 2023 to an expected >14% in 2026.

Segment performance: Taste sales +2% to $656M with EBITDA +18% to $153M; Food Ingredients sales +3% to $839M (volume +5%) with EBITDA +12% to $114M; Health & Biosciences sales +5% to $595M with EBITDA +7% to $153M; Scent sales +1% to $651M with EBITDA -2% to $148M.

Fragrance Ingredients (~$500M in external sales, roughly half specialty/half commodity) faces pressure from Indian and Chinese commodity producers, and IFF plans to deemphasize external commodity sales over the coming year, expecting the headwind to fade by 2027.
Vafseo and Auryxia generated $227 million in net product revenue in 2025, with total net product revenues increasing nearly 50% over calendar year 2024.

Cash and cash equivalents as of December 31, 2025, were $184.8 million compared to $51.9 million as of December 31, 2024, with management believing existing cash resources will fund operations for at least the next 2 years.
Net loss decreased significantly to $5.3 million in calendar year 2025 from a net loss of $69.4 million in calendar year 2024.

Vafseo demand was essentially flat at approximately $11-$12 million per quarter in Q2, Q3, and Q4 2025, with Q4 Vafseo net product revenue of $6.2 million negatively impacted by a onetime USRC inventory drawdown of approximately $4.8 million.

First refill adherence for Vafseo improved from approximately 75% for daily dosing patients in the first 9 months of 2025 to approximately 91% for observed dosing patients in Q4, and approximately 87% among a larger observed dosing subset in January 2026.

More than 1,000 prescribers at 24 different dialysis organizations have written a Vafseo prescription, and 290,000 patients now have access to Vafseo in dialysis clinics with a protocol in place, a nearly fivefold increase in prescriber access since end of Q3 2025.

Akebia expects generic competition for Auryxia to expand in 2026 beyond the current authorized generic, and therefore expects Auryxia revenues to decrease in 2026 compared to the $181.5 million generated in 2025.

A cost comparison analysis showed Vafseo had a 7.7% lower annual hospitalization rate, 16% reduction in hospitalization days, and approximately 15% lower Medicare hospitalization costs versus darbepoetin, translating to savings of about $3,700 per patient per year.

The company plans to initiate a Phase II open-label basket trial for AKB-097 (tissue-targeted complement inhibitor) in IgA nephropathy, lupus nephritis, and C3 glomerulopathy in the second half of 2026, with initial data expected in 2027.

Top-line data from the VOCAL study (evaluating Vafseo dosed 3 times weekly at DaVita clinics) are expected in Q4 2026, and results from the VOICE trial (evaluating Vafseo vs. standard of care on all-cause mortality and hospitalization) are expected in early 2027.
Worldwide Dupixent net sales for Q3 2025 were $4.9 billion, growing 26% year-over-year on a constant currency basis.
EYLEA HD U.S. net sales reached an all-time high of $431 million in Q3, with unit demand growing 18% quarter-over-quarter.
The FDA issued a complete response letter for the EYLEA HD prefilled syringe supplemental BLA due to unresolved inspection findings at the Catalent facility.
Regeneron expects a mid-teens percentage increase in R&D expense in 2026 relative to 2025 to support multiple large registrational programs.

The company anticipates returning approximately $4 billion to shareholders through dividends and repurchases in 2025, having already repurchased approximately $2.8 billion of shares through the first nine months of 2025.
The Sanofi development balance of approximately $900 million at quarter end is now expected to be fully reimbursed by no later than the end of Q3 2026.
Regeneron generated $3.2 billion in free cash flow through the first nine months of 2025 and ended the quarter with cash and marketable securities less debt of approximately $16 billion.

Global Libtayo net sales were $365 million, up 24% on a constant currency basis year-over-year, with the FDA approving Libtayo for high-risk adjuvant cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma earlier in October.
The Phase III pivotal trial results for fianlimab (LAG-3 antibody) in metastatic melanoma are now expected in the first half of 2026 due to slower event accrual.
Regeneron plans to invest over $7 billion in infrastructure and manufacturing facilities in New York and North Carolina over the coming years.

The FCC formally sent a draft Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRM) focused on PNT technology and solutions to the White House OMB earlier in March 2026, which the company describes as a critical step in the regulatory process.
NextNav finished Q4 2025 with approximately $152 million in cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments.
A significant number of warrants expiring in 2026 have the potential to deliver over $200 million in additional capital depending on stock price performance.
In Q4 2025, NextNav recognized approximately $48 million in noncash losses associated with the change in fair value of derivative and warrant liabilities.
The net loss for Q4 2025 was roughly $68 million, driven primarily by noncash derivative and warrant liability losses.
NextNav has begun operating what it describes as the world's first 5G-powered PNT network under an FCC experimental license in a defined geographic location, independent of the FCC's NPRM process.
NextNav announced an expanded partnership with Japan's MetCom, which has licensed NextNav's technology to power new terrestrial timing services in major Japanese metropolitan areas.
The company's proposed solution does not require taxpayer funding and management believes it can be made available during the current administration.
NextNav CEO Mariam Sorond joined the CTIA Board of Directors, positioning the company alongside major telecommunications industry leaders.

Lisa Hook was appointed as the Board's new Lead Independent Director, bringing experience as former CEO of publicly traded Neustar and expertise at the intersection of technology, telecommunications, and national security.

Q3 FY26 sales grew 19% organically year-over-year (22% reported including 5% FX tailwind), marking the third consecutive quarter of organic growth, with Infrastructure up 30% organically and Metal Cutting up 12%.

Adjusted EPS rose to $0.77 versus $0.47 in the prior-year quarter, and adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 20.8% from 17.9%, aided by $39 million of favorable price-raw timing in Infrastructure and $7 million of restructuring benefits.

Tungsten prices surged from approximately $900 to $3,000 per metric ton during the quarter (a roughly ninefold increase over the last 12 months), driven by supply constraints and Chinese export controls rather than higher demand.

Management raised FY26 guidance to sales of $2.33B–$2.35B and adjusted EPS of $3.75–$4.00, including approximately $2.45 of price-raw timing benefit (up $1.50 from the prior outlook), with Q4 net price and tariff surcharges expected to be ~35% year-over-year.

Year-to-date free operating cash flow fell to $18 million from $63 million, and full-year FY26 free operating cash flow is now expected to be approximately negative 30% of adjusted net income due to working capital pressure from rising tungsten costs.

Primary working capital climbed to $819 million (32.4% of sales) from $654 million year-over-year, and the company again suspended share repurchases (only $70M/3M shares of the $200M authorization used to date) pending tungsten price stabilization.

By end market on a constant currency basis, Earthworks grew 43%, Energy +28%, Aerospace & Defense +23%, General Engineering +14%, and Transportation +1%, with Americas up 27%, Asia Pacific up 25%, and EMEA up just 2%.

Management is delaying previously planned FY27 facility closures to prioritize growth opportunities, while still targeting ~$110 million of cumulative cost takeout savings by end of FY27 ($10M above the Investor Day target).

Preliminary FY27 framework implies a clean FY26 EPS baseline of about $1.63 (excluding $2.45 price-raw and $0.20 variable comp), plus $10M ($0.10) of additional restructuring savings, a $20 million variable compensation tailwind, with price-raw timing benefits concentrated in the first half (mostly Q1).

Aerospace & defense OEM build rates remain ~20% below pre-COVID levels and U.S. land rig counts are still ~30% below pre-COVID, but trailing 12-month unit volumes are up ~3% from the Q1 FY26 trough, marking the second consecutive quarter of year-over-year volume growth.
Oscar Health reported Q3 2025 total revenue of approximately $3 billion, a 23% increase year-over-year.
Q3 2025 medical loss ratio increased approximately 380 basis points year-over-year to 88.5% due to higher market morbidity.
The company's SG&A expense ratio improved by approximately 150 basis points year-over-year to 17.5% in Q3 2025.
Oscar reported a Q3 2025 net loss of $137 million and an adjusted EBITDA loss of $101 million.
Membership reached 2.1 million at quarter end, a 28% increase year-over-year.
The company completed a $410 million convertible notes offering due 2030, with net proceeds of $360 million after capped call transaction costs.
Oscar's weighted average rate increase for 2026 is approximately 28%, reflecting elevated trend and significantly higher market morbidity.
The company took actions to eliminate approximately $60 million in administrative costs for 2026.
Oscar ended Q3 with approximately $4.8 billion of cash and investments, including $541 million at the parent company and $564 million of excess capital at insurance subsidiaries.
Management expects the overall ACA market to contract by 20% to 30% in 2026 due to expiration of enhanced premium tax credits and program integrity efforts.
Q1 2026 consolidated net loss was $160 million with losses per share of $1.91 and EBITDA loss of $52 million, while adjusted EBITDA was $37 million and adjusted losses per share were $1.24.
CVR reinstated a quarterly dividend of $0.10 per share for Q1 2026, characterized by management as a regular (non-variable) dividend with intent to balance debt reduction and capital returns.

Q1 results included $158 million of unrealized derivative losses on NYMEX gasoline and diesel crack spread swaps covering 9.9 million barrels of diesel and 2.4 million barrels of gasoline, representing ~15% of 2026 expected production and ~4% of 2027.

Petroleum segment posted an adjusted EBITDA loss of $50 million (vs. $30 million loss YoY), with crude utilization of 97%, total throughput of ~214,000 bpd, and a realized margin of $4.72/bbl representing just a 22% capture rate on the Group 3 2-1-1.
Net RIN expense was $143 million ($7.37/bbl), negatively impacting capture rate by ~34%, with RIN prices more than doubling YoY to nearly $9.50/bbl and rising over 75% since the start of the year.

Fertilizer segment adjusted EBITDA rose to $78 million (vs. $53 million YoY) with ammonia utilization of 103%, and CVR Partners declared a $4/unit distribution generating ~$16 million in cash to CVR Energy.
Quarter-to-date Q2 2026 Group 2-1-1 cracks have averaged $38.36/bbl (vs. $21.58 in Q1), with prompt ammonia at $950/ton and UAN at $525/ton amid Middle East-driven supply disruptions.
The company is targeting gross leverage of $1 billion (excluding CVR Partners debt) and ended Q1 with consolidated cash of $512 million and total liquidity (ex-CVR Partners) of ~$923 million.
Full-year 2026 consolidated capital spending is guided at $200–$240 million, with Q2 petroleum throughput guided to 200,000–215,000 bpd and Q2 ammonia utilization guided to 95%–100%.

WCS exposure increased to ~18,000 bpd (~8% of slate vs. ~0% in Q4 2025) after the Western Canadian differential widened by ~$3/bbl following early-January Venezuela actions, and the EPA has again missed the deadline on Wynnewood's 2025 SRE petition, which if granted would have improved capture rate by ~12%.
Q1 2026 revenue was $11.1 million, down from $13.9 million year-over-year, a decrease of $2.8 million driven by lower volumes, less favorable waste mix, and delays in reaching key revenue milestones.

EBITDA from continuing operations was a loss of $7 million versus a $3.3 million loss in the prior year, with net loss of $7.5 million ($0.40 per share) compared to $3.6 million ($0.19 per share) last year.
Gross profit declined $3.5 million year-over-year due to lower revenue, higher variable costs in Treatment, and higher fixed plant costs incurred to prepare for anticipated higher volumes.
Cash ended the quarter at $6.7 million with working capital of $5.9 million, while cash used in operations was $3.6 million and investing activities used approximately $964,000.

Perma-Fix Northwest began receiving ETF waste from Hanford in mid-April, generating $1 million to $1.5 million per month and expected to support sustainable revenues of more than $4 million per quarter through at least Q3 into Q4.

The December 2025 permit renewal at Perma-Fix Northwest expanded permitted liquid mixed waste capacity to approximately 1.2 million gallons annually and authorizes treatment of up to 175,000 tons via macro encapsulation.

The EMF (DFLAW blowdown) waste stream is expected to begin in late June at roughly $300,000/month during hot commissioning, increasing 4x once DFLAW reaches operational phases anticipated in the fall.

The company has committed to DOE to install grouting capacity of 4.2 million gallons annually by October 2027 (within 18 months of a potential July 2026 award), targeting at least half of the West Side grouting opportunity tied to a $4 billion DOE contract for ~50 million gallons.

Perma-Fix was awarded a 2-year master task agreement valued at approximately $24 million from Lawrence Livermore National Security for building demolition and disposal, which mobilized in early April.

Treatment backlog ended the quarter at $12.2 million, up from $11.9 million at year-end and $10.2 million in Q1 2025, while SG&A rose ~$284,000 year-over-year to $4.3 million on higher labor, outside services, and marketing costs.

Clover Health grew Medicare Advantage membership 51% year-over-year to approximately 156,000 members, adding over 52,000 lives, and is now the largest PPO in New Jersey outside of special needs and employer retiree plans.
Q1 2026 total revenues were $749 million, up 62% year-over-year, with consolidated gross profit of $160 million, up 47% year-over-year.
GAAP net income was $27 million, a $29 million year-over-year improvement, and adjusted EBITDA was $40 million, up 56% year-over-year.
Insurance benefits expense ratio (BER) was 86.5% for the quarter, and management expects to deliver full-year 2026 GAAP net income profitability.
Adjusted SG&A was $119 million or 16% of revenue, improving roughly 200 basis points year-over-year versus prior guidance of 100-150 bps improvement for 2026.
Lower flu and COVID-related inpatient utilization contributed approximately 25 to 30 basis points of margin favorability versus 2025, while outpatient utilization and costs remain elevated.
Enrollment in Clover Care Services (home-based care) is up approximately 90% year-over-year, and over one-third of members received Clover Assistant-powered care during Q1.
The company ended Q1 with $418 million in total cash and investments, no debt outstanding, and generated $108 million of cash flow from operations.

Management intentionally moderated new member growth during OEP to prioritize clinical integration, and expects the 2025 cohort entering year three in 2027 to be a meaningful tailwind to margin and cash generation.

Management expects to meet or exceed full-year 2026 guidance across all metrics but will revisit guidance after Q2; Q1 included modest unfavorable prior-period development, contrasting with favorability in 2025.
Forestar generated $670.5 million in Q4 revenue (up 22% YoY) and $1.7 billion for fiscal 2025 (up 10% YoY), exceeding the high end of guidance.
Q4 net income increased 7% to $87 million ($1.70 per diluted share), while full-year net income was $167.9 million ($3.29 per diluted share).
Book value per share increased 11% year-over-year to $34.78, and has grown 92% over the last 5 years.
The company ended fiscal 2025 with $968 million of liquidity, including $379 million in cash and $589 million of available credit facility capacity.
Q4 gross profit margin was 22.3%, down 160 basis points from the prior year quarter due to an unusually high-margin project in the comparison period.
D.R. Horton started 15% of its homes on Forestar-developed lots in fiscal 2025, with a mutual goal to increase this to 33% (1 in 3 homes).
Forestar's lot position totaled 99,800 lots, with 23,800 owned lots (37% of owned supply) under contract expected to generate approximately $2.1 billion in future revenue.
For fiscal 2026, the company expects to deliver 14,000-15,000 lots and generate $1.6-$1.7 billion in revenue, with the second half expected to be stronger than the first half.
The company plans to invest approximately $1.4 billion in land acquisition and development in fiscal 2026, compared to $1.7 billion invested in fiscal 2025.
Total debt was $803 million with no senior note maturities until fiscal 2028, and net debt-to-capital ratio was 19.3%.
For Q3 2025, AFC generated distributable earnings of $0.16 per basic weighted average share of common stock and declared a dividend of $0.15 per common share.
Over 61% of outstanding shares were represented at the special meeting, with over 94% voting in favor of both proposals to convert from a REIT to a BDC.
The conversion to a BDC is anticipated to occur in the first quarter of 2026, and AFC will continue to trade under the NASDAQ ticker AFCG.
AFC received $43 million of principal repayments since the end of Q2, including a $23.2 million payoff from a private company term loan at par plus accrued interest.
The company has built a non-cannabis lending pipeline of approximately $350 million (out of a total pipeline of approximately $415 million), with target IRRs expected in the low double-digit range.
Due to an anticipated approximately $4 million taxable loss from the private company P settlement, the Board does not anticipate making a distribution to shareholders in Q4 2025.

As of September 30, 2025, CECL reserves were $51.3 million, or approximately 18.7% of loans at carrying value, plus an additional $31.2 million in total unrealized losses for loans held at fair value.
As of September 30, 2025, AFC had total assets of $288.7 million, total shareholder equity of $169.3 million, and book value per share of $7.49.
AFC ended Q3 2025 with $332.8 million of principal outstanding spread across 14 loans, reduced to $327.7 million across 14 loans as of November 3, 2025.
For Q3 2025, AFC reported net interest income of $6.5 million and a GAAP net loss of $12.5 million or $0.57 per basic weighted average share of common stock.
Latin America organic sales growth was 1.7%, including a 150 basis point negative impact from volume related to the Colgate Total formula replacement.
The Colgate Total formula change in Latin America created a gross margin impact of 40 to 50 basis points.
Hill's delivered 2.5% organic sales growth excluding private label, with private label exit creating approximately 300 basis points of negative impact in Q3.
Global categories are now growing roughly 2% compared to a 4% to 5% exit run rate in 2024.
Year-to-date gross profit margin is 60.1%, with full year gross margin expected to be roughly in line with that figure.
Full year organic sales growth is expected to be roughly in line with year-to-date at around 1.2%, including a 70 basis point impact from the exit of private label.
The Strategic Growth and Productivity Program has estimated charges of $200 million to $300 million, concluding by the end of 2028.
Mexico and Brazil both grew organic sales around 4% in the quarter.
India's GST tax on oral care and toothpaste decreased from 18% to 5%, leading to price reductions and trade inventory disruptions.
Colgate achieved positive pricing in every single division in the third quarter.
AMG generated full year 2025 economic earnings per share of $26.05, an increase of 22% year-over-year, which the company described as a record.
AMG affiliates generated approximately $29 billion in annual net client cash flows in 2025, the highest level since 2013, representing an organic growth rate of 4%.
AMG repurchased approximately $700 million of its shares in 2025, representing 11% of shares outstanding, with Q4 repurchases of $350 million being the largest quarterly amount in the firm's history.

AMG added approximately $97 billion in alternative AUM in 2025, representing a 35% increase in total alternative AUM, including $74 billion in net inflows from existing affiliates and $23 billion from new affiliate partnerships.
Alternative strategies now contribute approximately 60% of AMG's EBITDA on a run rate basis, up from roughly one-third six years ago, with affiliates managing $373 billion in alternative AUM.

AMG expects Q1 2026 economic earnings per share between $7.98 and $8.52, representing approximately 60% growth versus Q1 2025 at the midpoint, with fee-related earnings guidance of $270 million representing 30% expected growth.
AQR is expected to contribute more than 20% to AMG's earnings in 2026, up from a double-digit contribution in 2025, driven by strong organic growth and performance.

AMG received more than $730 million in pretax distributions and sale proceeds from liquidity events involving Peppertree, Comvest, and MBI, representing more than 2.5x invested capital with an average IRR exceeding 35%.

Global wealth AUM at AMG and affiliates now totals more than $100 billion and grew organically at more than 100% in 2025, with alternatives AUM on AMG's U.S. wealth platform reaching approximately $8 billion.

AMG anticipates repurchasing at least $400 million in shares in 2026 beyond the $174 million conversion premium on trust preferred securities and expects net performance fee earnings of approximately $170 million for 2026.
Q2 revenue increased 8% year-over-year to $200 million, exceeding guidance by $3 million.
Net new ARR in Q2 was $14 million, the largest organic increase in the past 7 quarters, with year-on-year ARR growth of 7%.
Million-dollar plus subscription customers increased 5% sequentially to a new high of 132.
GAAP operating income more than doubled year-over-year with margin expanding by 7 points to a record quarterly high.
Marketplace and other revenue increased 18% to $50 million, with Data Marketplace (75% of segment) growing 14%.
Total RPO (contracted backlog) increased 29% to $652 million and current RPO increased 15% to $430 million.
Free cash flow was $57 million in Q2, with $50 million deployed toward share repurchases and $80 million repurchased fiscal year-to-date.
Company raised FY '26 revenue guidance to $804-$818 million, representing 8-10% growth, while reiterating non-GAAP operating income guidance of $178-$182 million.
Balance sheet remains strong with $377 million in cash and short-term investments and zero debt.
Company expects stock-based compensation to decline 23% year-over-year to $83 million, and projects GAAP operating margin of 10-11% for FY '26, an increase of 9-10 points year-over-year.
Q4 2025 net revenue was $29.6 million, a 14.1% increase over the prior year period, making it the company's strongest quarter of the year.

Q4 firearm sales were $25.7 million, reflecting a 19.1% increase driven by 11.5% volume growth, significantly outpacing the broader industry as adjusted NICS background checks declined 4.1% during the same period.
Q4 gross profit margin expanded 290 basis points to 15.9%, driven by onetime purchasing opportunities, favorable product mix, and strengthened supplier relationships.
Full year 2025 revenues were $96.4 million, representing 3.6% growth, with gross profit margin improving to 11.7% from 10.4% in the prior year.
The company ended 2025 with $110.4 million in cash and cash equivalents and minimal debt, with cash position increasing during Q4 due to positive operating cash flow.
The company repurchased approximately 1.56 million shares for $8.9 million in 2025, with $11.1 million remaining under the current repurchase authorization entering 2026.

PEW Logistics delivered over 500 orders and approximately $400,000 in gross merchandise value in its first 30 days, exceeding internal projections, with a 1% e-commerce conversion rate already outpacing the traditional online firearms retail benchmark.
Mobile engagement accounted for 72% of traffic and 64% of revenue in 2025, up 19% and 11% year-over-year respectively, with mobile driving higher conversion rates.
The company acquired a new headquarters and fulfillment facility for $8.25 million at approximately 2.5x its current footprint, expected to be fully operational in Q4 2026.
Management expects operations to be approximately cash flow neutral in 2026, with cash deployment directed toward strategic share repurchases, technology investments, and potential acquisitions.

3M delivered Q4 2025 organic growth of 2.2%, operating margin of 21.1%, EPS of $1.83, and free cash flow conversion of over 130%.

The company plans gross share repurchases of approximately $2.5 billion in 2026.
Potential new tariffs on Europe trade flows could result in a $30-40 million impact in 2026 if enacted as proposed, though this is not included in current guidance.
Total company revenues for Q2 fiscal 2026 reached $5.18 billion, a 2% increase from the prior year quarter.
Distribution revenues grew 4% during the quarter, with subscriber declines improving to 6.3%, excluding FOX One contributions.
Tubi delivered its most streamed quarter ever with total view time up 27% year-over-year and revenue growing 19%, achieving EBITDA profitability for the second consecutive quarter.
Fiscal year-to-date, Fox repurchased $1.8 billion through its share buyback program, bringing cumulative repurchases to $8.4 billion or approximately 35% of total shares outstanding since 2019.
Quarterly adjusted EBITDA was $692 million compared to $781 million in the prior year quarter, with adjusted EPS of $0.82.
FOX News scatter pricing is up 46-47% year-on-year, and the company added approximately 200 new advertisers in the first half on top of 350 new advertisers added last year.
Total minutes viewed across Sports, News, Entertainment and Tubi increased 15% year-over-year in calendar year 2025.
The company ended the quarter with approximately $2 billion in cash and $6.6 billion in debt, and announced a $0.28 per share semiannual dividend.
FOX News Digital social media views were up 170% over the prior year, and the network finished the quarter as the most watched cable network in total day.
The company's 2.5% stake in Flutter is worth approximately $700 million, and the 18.6% option in FanDuel is valued at approximately $2.1 billion based on average buy-side valuations.

Investment services fees from Securities Services and Market and Wealth Services segments grew 10% year-over-year, driven by net new business, higher client activity, and market values.
Net interest income of $1.2 billion was up 18% year-over-year, and full year 2025 NII is expected to be up 12% year-over-year.
Firm-wide AUC/A of $57.8 trillion increased 11% year-over-year, with ETF AUC/A up 35% year-over-year.

CET1 ratio increased to 11.7% from 11.5% in the prior quarter, while full year expenses are expected to be up approximately 3% year-over-year.
117 AI solutions are now in production, up 75% from the prior quarter, with over 100 digital employees working alongside staff on tasks.
Non-trust bank platform-like businesses now represent approximately two-thirds of pre-tax income, up from 55% three years ago.
The number of clients buying three or more BNY services is up 40% over the past two years, with almost half of Asset Servicing wins in the quarter representing multiline of business solutions.
F5 exceeded $3 billion in revenue and $1 billion in operating profit for the first time in FY'25, with revenue growing 10% and EPS growing 18% year-over-year.
Record free cash flow of $906 million was generated in FY'25, up 19% compared to FY'24, resulting in a free cash flow margin of 29%.

FY'26 revenue guidance of 0% to 4% growth reflects potential near-term disruption from the August 9 security incident, compared to mid-single-digit growth the business was otherwise tracking toward.
Software revenue grew 9% year-over-year to $803 million in FY'25, with term-based subscriptions up 18% to $508 million.
Total security revenue grew 6% to approximately $1.2 billion, representing 39% of total FY'25 revenue.
Nearly 900 customers were leveraging F5 XOps capabilities by the end of Q4, up from just 20 customers in 2024.
26% of F5's top 1,000 customers are now using F5 Distributed Cloud Services, up from 17% in 2024.
More than half of F5's installed base remains on legacy systems nearing end of software support, indicating the tech refresh opportunity is still in early stages.
F5 secured AI use case wins with more than 30 customers in FY'25, representing net new insertion points across AI data delivery, AI runtime security, and AI factory load balancing.

The company issued 2026 guidance of $280 million to $300 million in revenue, representing 12% to 20% year-over-year base business growth, with adjusted EBITDA loss of $15 million to $25 million.
Medical Transportation business is expected to generate more than $200 million of revenue in 2025 and achieved record volumes in Q3.
The company assigned over 26,000 trips to other vendors over the last 12 months due to capacity constraints and plans to hire 700 to 800 additional EMS staff to capture this embedded demand.
SteadyMD acquisition adds a 50-state virtual care network with over 500 clinicians, projected to generate approximately $25 million in revenue in 2025 and service over 3 million patients.
Remote patient monitoring is operating at an annual run rate of approximately $15 million with greater than 10% adjusted EBITDA contribution margin.
The company paid off the $30 million outstanding balance on its credit line during Q3, making the balance sheet debt-free for the first time since late 2023.
Total cash and cash equivalents, including restricted cash and investments, was $95.2 million as of September 30, 2025, with expected exit cash of approximately $65 million at the end of 2026.
The company has collected approximately 96% of all migrant-related receivables from inception, with approximately $37 million remaining at quarter end compared to $150 million at the end of 2024.
Rigel reported full year 2025 net product sales of $232 million, an increase of $87 million or 60% compared to 2024.
The company provided 2026 total revenue guidance of $275 million to $290 million, comprising $255 million to $265 million in net product sales and $20 million to $25 million in contract revenues.
Rigel ended 2025 with cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments of $155 million compared to $77.3 million at the end of 2024.
TAVALISSE achieved record Q4 2025 net product sales of $45.6 million, a 47% increase year-over-year.
In the Phase Ib dose escalation study of R289, 6 of 18 evaluable patients (33%) receiving doses of 500 mg daily or higher achieved red cell transfusion independence lasting 8 weeks or longer.

A noncash deferred income tax benefit of $245.9 million was recognized in Q4 2025 due to the release of the valuation allowance on deferred tax assets, driving reported full year net income to $367 million.
Based on the midpoint of 2026 net product sales guidance of $260 million, Rigel has achieved a compound annual growth rate of approximately 35% since 2022.

GAVRETO generated over $40 million in full year 2025 sales compared to approximately $28 million to $30 million under the prior company, with Q4 net product sales of $10.2 million, up 27% year-over-year.
Rigel expects to select the recommended Phase II dose for R289 in the second half of 2026 and share top line data from the dose expansion phase by the end of the year.

Full year 2025 total costs and expenses were $168.8 million compared to $155.1 million in 2024, with the increase primarily driven by higher R&D costs related to R289 and olutasidenib clinical activities.
Elanco delivered 9% organic constant currency revenue growth in Q3 2025, marking 9 consecutive quarters of underlying total growth.
The company raised its full year innovation revenue guidance by $100 million at the midpoint to $840 million to $880 million, with year-to-date innovation revenue reaching $655 million.
Credelio Quattro became Elanco's fastest pet health blockbuster in history, reaching $100 million in net sales in less than 8 months with only a single geographic approval.

The company refinanced its $2.1 billion Term Loan B facility, extending maturities through 2032, though interest expense is expected to increase by approximately $15 million year-over-year in 2026.
U.S. Farm Animal delivered 20% growth in Q3 on top of 11% growth in Q3 2024, with Experior growing 70% in Q3 on top of more than 100% growth in Q3 2024.
Zenrelia is now in over 12,000 U.S. clinics (up from 10,000 in August) with a reorder rate over 80%, and approximately 18% of Zenrelia patients are new to therapy.
Full year 2025 guidance was raised to organic constant currency growth of 6% to 6.5%, adjusted EBITDA of $880 million to $900 million, and adjusted EPS of $0.91 to $0.94.
Gross debt paydown of $562 million has already exceeded the 2025 target, with cash generated from operations of $219 million in Q3 compared to $162 million in Q3 2024.
The broad spectrum endecto market has grown to $1.4 billion with growth at almost 40%, and Zenrelia has achieved double-digit percent market share in Japan, Brazil, and Canada.
Q1 2026 comparable diluted EPS came in at $0.94, up 22% year-over-year, with comparable operating earnings up 10% year-over-year on global volume growth of approximately 1%.

EMEA segment comparable operating earnings rose 20% in Q1 on low-single-digit volume growth, with less than half of the operating earnings gain attributable to FX translation (about $15 million company-wide FX benefit).

Broadridge delivered Q2 recurring revenue growth of 8% constant currency and adjusted EPS of $1.59, with the company raising its adjusted EPS growth guidance to 9% to 12% from 8% to 12%.
Total equity position growth was 17% with revenue position growth at 11%, and fund position growth strengthened from 2% in Q1 to 15% in Q2.
Broadridge recorded a $187 million noncash mark-to-market gain related to digital asset holdings, with the value of digital asset holdings rising to $265 million at quarter end.

The Distributed Ledger Repo (DLR) platform tokenized $384 billion per day in December or $9 trillion for the month, more than double the volumes from June.

Seven dairy digester LCFS pathways were approved at an average negative 384 carbon intensity score, increasing LCFS credit revenue by 160% for these dairies starting in Q3 2025.
The $30 million Mechanical Vapor Recompression system is expected to reduce natural gas use by 80% and add an estimated $32 million in annual cash flow starting mid-2026.

Interest expense remained steady at approximately $13 million during the quarter, with about $118 million of debt at an effective interest rate of approximately 5.1% and expensive debt refinancing in process.

India biofuels posted $14.5 million of revenues, with the company targeting an IPO of the India subsidiary in early 2026 at a valuation range of $100 million to $300 million, seeking to sell 20-25% of the subsidiary.
Cash at quarter end was $5.6 million after making $4.1 million of investments into carbon intensity reduction and dairy renewable natural gas production expansion during the quarter.
California's recent E15 approval is expected to increase ethanol demand by more than 600 million gallons per year and decrease fuel prices at the pump by $2.7 billion per year when fully adopted.
LCFS credit prices have risen by more than 25% since summer and are expected to continue increasing toward the cap of $268, which continues to increase each year.

Gogo shipped over 200 HDX units year-to-date, nearly 3x the 77 shipments announced on the Q2 call, with 93% earmarked for specific customers.
5G flight testing began on October 28 with results exceeding expectations, and the company plans to begin shipping boxes to 400 pre-provisioned 5G customers in early Q1 2025.
Total ATG aircraft online at the end of Q3 was 6,529, a decline of approximately 7% versus the prior year period and down 3% sequentially.

Gogo achieved over $30 million of annualized synergies and expects run rate synergies to modestly exceed the previous range of $30 million to $35 million, up from original guidance of $25 million to $30 million.
Q3 free cash flow was $31 million, above expectations, totaling $94 million year-to-date, with the company reiterating the high end of the $60 million to $90 million full-year range.
FDX will be a LEO line-fit option for all new Bombardier Challenger and global business aircraft types, with revenue generation expected in early 2027.

Military/government revenue, currently 13% of total revenue, is expected to move towards 20% over the longer term, including a recently announced $33 million ceiling value contract with SES Space & Defense.
